page: Amazon Web Services r8idb.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel x86_64 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz, providing 16 virtual CPUs across 8 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance is provisioned with 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU to support workloads requiring substantial in-memory capacity.

Integrated hardware includes 950 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a baseline network throughput of 17 Gbps. This instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators. The combination of local NVMe storage and dedicated core allocation facilitates low-latency I/O operations directly on the physical host, bypassing network-attached storage bottlenecks for temporary data structures.

From an architectural standpoint, bundling dedicated local high-speed storage with a high memory-to-vCPU ratio delivers cost efficiency for heavy data processing without necessitating auxiliary block storage volumes. However, as instance store volumes are ephemeral, persistent state requires robust application-level replication or external storage architectures.

Workloads best aligned with the hardware profile of the r8idb.4xlarge include in-memory databases, memory-bound caching systems, distributed data processing nodes, and transactional database engines that utilize local flash storage for scratch disks or write-ahead logging.

The r8idb.4xlarge is appropriate for in-memory caching systems, transactional databases, and real-time analytical workloads requiring fast local scratch storage.
